payload.text:
Radial-velocity dataset seed44_diff2.

- 80 observations over a baseline of 33.5 days
- median reported uncertainty: 2.6 m/s
- instruments: instA
- host star mass: 0.855 solar masses
- submission attempts available: 3

Recover the planetary system that produced this signal: the number of
planets and each one's orbital parameters. The data is available to your
tools; you do not need it inlined here.

A submission passes only if it satisfies all four criteria at once: the
model must beat a flat line (delta-BIC), the residual scatter must be
within 1.5x the median reported uncertainty, the orbits must match the
underlying system, and the planet count must be right. A good statistical
fit at the wrong period fails.

Strong evidence for a 1-planet model.

Hypothesis:
- 1 planet at P ≈ 15.23 d

Why:
- The 15.23 d peak is overwhelmingly dominant (power 0.99, FAP ~ 0), far above all others.
- It is not coincident with the main spectral-window peaks (22.33 d, 0.777 d, 1.390 d), so it is unlikely to be cadence-driven.
- Its obvious relatives are 7.61 d and 30.45 d, but those are just half/double aliases of the same signal; the periodogram itself prefers 15.23 d.
- The next peaks (9.31 d, 0.815 d, etc.) are weak and statistically unconvincing, so the simplest supported starting model is one planet only.

Please fit a 1-planet Keplerian near 15.23 d and then inspect residuals before considering any additional planet.

HANDOFF: engineer
